newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end Tokyo slightly up, rise capped around 125.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end Tokyo slightly up, rise capped around 125.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures closed slightly firmer on Friday after hitting a strong barrier just above 125.00.
Trade was subdued amid a lack of fresh factors, but sentiment remained basically bullish after the contract was buoyed by late bargain-hunting in cash bonds on Thursday.

"What investors currently have in their mind is that they want to buy when the September is around 124.50 and sell when the September rises to 125.50. Dealers, thus, tend to take profits before the September rises above 125.00," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
The September ended up 0.02 at 124.91 after moving between 124.88 and 125.09.
An early fall in Tokyo stocks briefly boosted JGBs as did a decline in short-term cash interest rates and a dip in interest rate swap (IRS) rates, traders said.
One-month certificates of deposit rate fell to 0.58 percent from Thursday's 0.59 percent.
City banks were said to have continued buying fixed interest rates in the IRS market, in an apparent attempt to increase capital gains, traders said.

"Vague fears over Japan's financial system in relation to an increase in financially troubled companies have prompted buying at the short-end of the yen interest rate yield curve," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
Many market operators are now firmly fixed in their view that the Bank of Japan will not be able to raise interest rates immediately, traders said.

The recent weakness in Tokyo stocks, especially in the construction sector, led to this view, they said. Yaohan Japan Corp and contractor Aoki Corp were among companies which saw their shares sold heavily on Friday.
But the demand/supply balance of the JGB market remained off keel after a flood of long-term corporate bond launches this week, and this kept the topside capped, traders said.

"For example, investors didn't buy the electric power firm's long-term bond when it was launched with tight terms. But they started to buy when the spread of the bond yield against JGBs widened to 15 basis points," the first dealer said. Tokyo Electric Power Co Ltd (TEPCO) launched 100 billion yen worth of 10-year straight bonds on Tuesday. TEPCO set the coupon rate at 2.625 percent, only six basis points above the equivalent 197th 10-year JGB.
Traders said the activity of institutional investors was negligible, especially at the long-end.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB was down 0.005 at 2.280 percent at 0742 GMT.

Some dealers said lending rates for the 4.6 percent 174th 10-year JGB, which is the cheapest to deliver (CTD) cash issue for the September, were up on Friday, probably due to demand from foreign operators. But others said short-squeezing of the 174th issue was unlikely, as it was a former benchmark bond with a large issue amount.
